## Motivation KDA’s chunked prefill path currently materializes contiguous Q/K/V tensors and normalizes Q and K through separate operations. For strided QKV inputs, this introduces redundant intermediate memory traffic and multiple kernel launches. This PR combines QKV materialization and Q/K L2 normalization into one Triton kernel, reducing preparation overhead while preserving the existing numerical behavior. ## Modifications - Add a fused Triton kernel that reads strided Q/K/V directly, applies Q/K L2 normalization, and produces contiguous Q/K/V outputs. - Preserve the reference FP32 reduction, normalization, and BF16 output conversion. - Add an opt-in path controlled by SGLANG_KDA_FUSED_QKV_PACK=1, disabled by default. - Restrict the fused path to supported CUDA BF16 layouts with batch dimension 1 and head dimension 128. Unsupported configurations retain the existing implementation. - Keep the optimization independent of CP and MoE optimizations. - Add regression tests for output equivalence, CUDA Graph replay, KDA state updates, and fallback behavior. ## Accuracy Tests 9 GPU regression tests passed on NVIDIA H200 Coverage includes: - Bitwise equivalence against the separate preparation operations for sequence lengths 1, 65, 4237, and 32768. - CUDA Graph replay correctness after updating inputs. - Full KDA output, SSM state, and tracked-state equivalence for single- and multi-sequence inputs. - Fallback behavior for unsupported layouts, including head dimension 64. ```bash python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_qkv_pack.py ``` This validation covers operator and KDA integration correctness; no model-level accuracy evaluation was performed for this PR. ## Speed Tests and Profiling

Microbenchmarks were run on NVIDIA H200 using BF16 strided QKV inputs with 16 heads and head dimension 128.

Timing uses CUDA Events around CUDA Graph replay, with 21 alternating baseline/fused samples and 20 replays per sample. Reported latency is the median.

Tokens| Separate preparation | Fused preparation | Speedup | Latency reduction --| -- | -- | -- | -- 4237 | 80.15 μs | 27.88 μs | 2.87× | 65.2% 8192 | 153.83 μs | 51.17 μs | 3.01× | 66.7% 32167 | 570.04 μs | 191.37 μs | 2.98× | 66.4% 32768 | 580.29 μs | 194.82 μs | 2.98× | 66.4%

The fused implementation replaces Q/K contiguous copies, two L2-normalization kernels, and the V contiguous copy with a single kernel.

These measurements cover QKV preparation only, excluding subsequent KDA computation. They do not represent whole-layer or end-to-end speedups.

## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. @@ -44,6 +45,8 @@
 # log2(e) rounded to fp32, matching flash-linear-attention.

 def cdiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:

@@ -1296,7 +1299,20 @@ def chunk_kda(

@@ -0,0 +1,99 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Normalize strided KDA Q/K and pack V without temporary Q/K copies."""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["ROWS"])
+def _kda_qkv_pack(
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    qo,
+    ko,
+    vo,
+    eps,
+    ROWS,
+    qs_t: tl.constexpr,
+    qs_h: tl.constexpr,
+    ks_t: tl.constexpr,
+    ks_h: tl.constexpr,
+    vs_t: tl.constexpr,
+    vs_h: tl.constexpr,
+    H: tl.constexpr,
+    D: tl.constexpr,
+    BT: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    rows = tl.program_id(0) * BT + tl.arange(0, BT)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, D)
+    mask = rows[:, None] < ROWS
+    token = rows // H
+    head = rows % H
+    qval = tl.load(
+        q + token[:, None] * qs_t + head[:, None] * qs_h + cols[None, :],
+        mask=mask,
+        other=0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    kval = tl.load(
+        k + token[:, None] * ks_t + head[:, None] * ks_h + cols[None, :],
+        mask=mask,
+        other=0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    vval = tl.load(
+        v + token[:, None] * vs_t + head[:, None] * vs_h + cols[None, :],
+        mask=mask,
+        other=0,
+    )
+    # Match l2norm_fwd_kernel's FP32 reduction/division and BF16 store.
+    qnorm = qval / tl.sqrt(tl.sum(qval * qval, axis=1) + eps)[:, None]
+    knorm = kval / tl.sqrt(tl.sum(kval * kval, axis=1) + eps)[:, None]
+    offsets = rows[:, None] * D + cols[None, :]
+    tl.store(qo + offsets, qnorm.to(qo.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+    tl.store(ko + offsets, knorm.to(ko.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+    tl.store(vo + offsets, vval, mask=mask)
+
+
+def supports_kda_qkv_pack(q, k, v):
+    return (
+        q.is_cuda
+        and q.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and q.ndim == 4
+        and q.shape[0] == 1
+        and q.shape[1] > 0
+        and q.shape == k.shape == v.shape
+        and q.shape[-1] == 128
+        and q.device == k.device == v.device
+        and q.dtype == k.dtype == v.dtype
+        and q.stride(-1) == k.stride(-1) == v.stride(-1) == 1
+    )
+
+
+def kda_qkv_pack(q, k, v, eps=1e-6):
+    assert supports_kda_qkv_pack(q, k, v)
+    result = torch.empty((3, *q.shape), device=q.device, dtype=q.dtype)
+    qo, ko, vo = result.unbind(0)
+    rows = q.shape[1] * q.shape[2]
+    _kda_qkv_pack[(triton.cdiv(rows, 16),)](
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        qo,
+        ko,
+        vo,
+        eps,
+        ROWS=rows,
+        qs_t=q.stride(1),
+        qs_h=q.stride(2),
+        ks_t=k.stride(1),
+        ks_h=k.stride(2),
+        vs_t=v.stride(1),
+        vs_h=v.stride(2),
+        H=q.shape[2],
+        D=128,
+        BT=16,
+        num_warps=8,
+        num_stages=3,
+    )
+    return qo, ko, vo

@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+"""Regression tests for optional strided KDA preparation, including state writes."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla import kda
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.kda_qkv_pack import (
+    kda_qkv_pack,
+    supports_kda_qkv_pack,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.l2norm import l2norm_fwd
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=180, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("length", [1, 65, 4237, 32768])
+def test_strided_pack_bit_parity_and_graph(length):
+    torch.manual_seed(45)
+    x = torch.randn((1, length, 6144), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    q, k, v = [z.unflatten(-1, (16, 128)) for z in x.chunk(3, dim=-1)]
+
+    def reference():
+        return l2norm_fwd(q.contiguous()), l2norm_fwd(k.contiguous()), v.contiguous()
+
+    actual = kda_qkv_pack(q, k, v)
+    for a, b in zip(actual, reference()):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(a, b, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        replay = kda_qkv_pack(q, k, v)
+    x.mul_(0.5)
+    graph.replay()
+    for a, b in zip(replay, reference()):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(a, b, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "lengths,dim", [([65], 128), ([65, 67], 128), ([4237], 128), ([65], 64)]
+)
+def test_complete_kda_state_and_track_parity(monkeypatch, lengths, dim):
+    torch.manual_seed(46)
+    total = sum(lengths)
+    mixed = (
+        torch.randn((1, total, 3 * 16 * dim), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1
+    )
+    q, k, v = [z.unflatten(-1, (16, dim)) for z in mixed.chunk(3, dim=-1)]
+    gate = -torch.rand((1, total, 16, dim), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.02
+    beta = torch.randn((1, total, 16), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    cu = torch.tensor(
+        [0] + list(__import__("itertools").accumulate(lengths)),
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+    )
+    pool = (
+        torch.randn((4, 2, 16, dim, dim), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.001
+    )
+    indices = torch.tensor([3, 1][: len(lengths)], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+    snapshots = torch.tensor([0] * len(lengths), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    def run(enabled):
+        state = pool.clone()[:, 0]
+        track = torch.zeros(
+            (len(lengths), 16, dim, dim), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32
+        )
+        monkeypatch.setattr(kda, "_FUSE_KDA_QKV_PACK", enabled)
+        output = kda.chunk_kda(
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            gate,
+            beta,
+            initial_state=state,
+            initial_state_indices=indices,
+            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+            cu_seqlens=cu,
+            beta_is_raw=True,
+            track_state=track,
+            track_chunk_idx=snapshots,
+        )
+        return output, state, track
+
+    before = run(False)
+    after = run(True)
+    for a, b in zip(after, before):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(a, b, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+def test_unsupported_layout_guard():
+    cpu = torch.zeros((1, 1, 16, 128), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    assert not supports_kda_qkv_pack(cpu, cpu, cpu)
+    x = torch.zeros((1, 1, 16, 64), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    assert not supports_kda_qkv_pack(x, x, x)

Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
